why: ptja/PTJA-FINDINGS.json records Wave 3 as NOT PERFORMED: 125 of 129 verifier agents died on session limits, so every Wave 2 conclusion is hunter-reproduced and never independently confirmed. Nine of those conclusions are REFUTATIONS - findings closed with 'this is actually safe' - and all nine named ZERO executable tests. A refutation with no test is an opinion. This is the audit's own defect class, unknown-or-absent treated as satisfied, pointed at the audit's own conclusions.

findings_verified.claim: signature is verified before any state change, and an absent or whitespace-only signing secret fails closed
cases: A1-01 unsigned capture refused 400, no durable state
A1-02 wrongly signed capture refused 401, no durable state
A1-03 sign-then-swap: a signature over a different body does not validate the swapped body
A1-04 no secret configured -> 503, nothing processed
A1-05 whitespace-only secret reads as absent -> 503 (the specifically named claim)
A1-06 live mode without the approval flag refuses whatever secrets exist
A1-07 approved live with no live secret refuses rather than falling back
A1-08 approved live does NOT accept a sandbox-signed payload (credential separation)
A1-10 a truncated signature is not prefix-matched
A1-11 an absent event id is refused before any state change
A1-09 NON-VACUITY: a correctly signed capture IS processed and does write state
findings_verified.assertion_strength: every refusal case asserts BOTH the status AND that payment_gateway_events, payment_reconciliation_records and payment_exceptions are all empty. The status alone was not accepted as proof that no state changed.

findings_verified.claim: an equal event id replayed as a DIFFERENT event type does not re-run the money path
cases: A2-01 capture id replayed as refund.processed -> duplicate, no money figure moves, no second event row
A2-02 same id same type -> idempotent no-op, capture not recounted
A2-03 NON-VACUITY: a refund under a FRESH id does run the refund path and does record refunded_amount

sabotage.control: the safeEqual signature comparison in app/api/razorpay-webhook/route.ts
the .trim() in payment-webhook-gate val(), so a whitespace secret reads as configured
the duplicate event-id guard in processGatewayEvent

shadowing_caught_and_fixed: A2-01 first passed while proving nothing: with no internal booking_refund_cases row the refund died as orphan_gateway_refund anyway, so the replay guard was never exercised. Fixed by seeding a real refund case AND linking the gateway order, so the refund would genuinely land if the guard let it through.

A2-03, the non-vacuity control, FAILED on first run - which is what exposed the above. A refund event carries its booking only on the refund entity and extract() reads notes from the payment/order/payment_link entities, so refunds resolve through payment_gateway_links. The fixture had never created one.
observation_not_a_finding: A refund webhook arriving before any payment_gateway_links row exists resolves to unmatched_gateway_event and is raised to the ops exception queue rather than being applied. That is the fail-closed direction and is correct; it is recorded here only because it is the reason the first non-vacuity run read refunded_amount 0.
not_claimed: No live or sandbox Razorpay traffic was involved. No credential exists in any environment. This verifies the RECEIVER's behaviour against crafted payloads, not the gateway integration.
The other seven Wave 2 refutations remain unverified at the time of this entry.
